assets.purpose: Illustrative stamped query, cleaned candidate, separate variable genuine reference.
assets.final_prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Edit target: the attached three-panel signature workflow illustration. Preserve the polished white panoramic layout, burgundy DEMO stamp, navy arrows, invented signature style and realistic ink texture. Regenerate the illustration with the following scientifically important distinction.
LEFT panel and MIDDLE panel are the SAME QUERY before and after illustrative stamp cleaning: retain the same underlying query handwriting geometry in those two panels, with residual pale stamp traces in the middle. Cleaning is only an illustrative candidate.
RIGHT panel compares TWO DIFFERENT genuine signing instances from the same invented writer. The upper CLEAN REFERENCE must be visibly but subtly different from the query shown on the left and middle. Make its opening loop slightly narrower and more upright, vary the height and spacing of the small middle strokes, shift the baseline mildly and make the long final stroke and terminal flourish modestly shorter and at a slightly different angle. Preserve enough common personal style that the samples plausibly belong to the same writer. These must look like natural repeated handwriting, NOT exact pixel copies, NOT a completely different writer, and NOT just rotation or scale of the same signature.
The lower right sample is the cleaned query from the middle panel. The bracket compares that query with the independently written upper reference. Keep the variations clearly visible at publication size.
No authenticity verdict, no confidence number, no green check. Only readable text is DEMO inside the fictional stamp. No titles or captions within the image. Maintain the 3:1 wide composition and generous white margins.
The central lesson: a real verifier must tolerate natural within-writer variation; matching does not mean identical handwriting.

assets.purpose: Conceptual literature overview in a journal-style scientific illustration.
assets.final_prompt:
Scientific educational illustration of machine-learning ideas from nine research papers.
Style reference only: the attached journal illustration's delicate outlines, translucent salmon feature-map slabs, light green pooling blocks, pale gold embedding vectors, lavender output symbols and white background. Create an original composition. Do not reproduce the journal page, original figure, real handwriting, identity documents, stamps or seals.
Use abstract, obviously artificial black pen-stroke shapes as synthetic research inputs; they must not spell a person's name. The six vignettes are independent literature themes, not a single connected model.
Arrange six beautifully drawn miniature scientific illustrations in a panoramic 2-row, 3-column layout, approximately 3:1 aspect ratio. No rounded flowchart boxes, no card backgrounds, no central hub. Large visual elements and short legible navy labels.
Top row:
"P1  Real documents" — two abstract pen-stroke crops with background interference shown as a translucent burgundy geometric ring.
"F0  P5  P8  Learned features" — two naturally different abstract stroke samples leading through dimensional convolution and pooling slabs into small gold feature vectors.
"P2  Local and global" — one stroke sample with a local convolution branch and a patch-token attention branch, with vectors combined.
Bottom row:
"P6  Regional comparison" — paired synthetic stroke strips with three corresponding image regions linked by fine comparison lines.
"P3  P4  Document restoration" — a research illustration of separating a colored interference layer from a document-content layer; conceptual layers only, no manipulation of a real document.
"P7  Covariance features" — gradient samples, a symmetric matrix and a geometric distance arc.
Use only those six labels as text. No numerical network dimensions, scores, performance claims or authenticity verdicts. This is conceptual background art for an academic proposal, not an operational system or experiment. Refined, professionally typeset, crisp, technically coherent and readable when printed at 16 cm wide.

assets.purpose: Shared paired regional verification with query visibility, optional restoration, and reference aggregation.
assets.base_prompt:
Create an original professional journal-style illustration of a proposed research system for comparing synthetic handwriting images under visual interference. White background, fine black technical outlines, perspective translucent salmon convolutional feature maps, green pooling planes, gold vectors, lavender scalar score symbols, and burgundy reliability information, inspired by the supplied STYLE reference only. Not a generic rounded-box flowchart. Use a broad landscape 2:1 composition and large print-readable labels.
For scientific clarity show EXACTLY ONE reference–query comparison, repeated across references as a written label. Do not draw three independent reference pipelines.
Upper-left synthetic handwriting thumbnail labelled "Reference". Lower-left naturally different handwriting thumbnail in the same fictional style with translucent burgundy interference labelled "Query". No real name, identity document or seal.
Both inputs feed identical-looking convolution and pooling stacks, one above the other, labelled together "Shared encoder". Each stream ends in one feature map with exactly three colored region windows. A dashed connector between the encoder streams means "Shared weights".
In the CENTER show exactly THREE regional comparisons stacked vertically. Each comparison consists of one small reference feature cube above one small query feature cube of the same color. A connector from BOTH cubes converges to ONE lavender comparison symbol. There must be exactly three comparison outputs in total, one per region. Label the group "Regional similarities". Never send an individual image feature directly to score fusion.
Those THREE lavender comparison outputs feed ONE gold fusion bar labelled "Regional fusion". Below the original Query thumbnail show a burgundy interference heatmap labelled "Visibility estimate". Its arrow feeds the Regional fusion bar as weights.
The fused score then points to a second small gold aggregation element labelled "Across references", then to one neutral lavender output labelled "Assessment or review". A small note near the comparison reads "Repeat for each reference".
A thin optional preprocessing branch below the Query shows schematic colored interference and content layers separating. Label it "Optional restoration". Its dashed return arrow must enter the short QUERY INPUT arrow BEFORE the FIRST convolution slab. It must not enter any internal feature stage. The direct Query-to-encoder arrow remains visible.
The inference order is strict: reference and query -> shared feature extraction -> paired corresponding-region similarities -> weighted regional fusion -> aggregate across references -> assessment/review. Visibility is estimated from the original query. Restoration is optional.
Use only the short labels given above, no dimensions, accuracy numbers, class counts, percentages, approval ticks or authenticity verdicts. Use dimensional neural feature-map drawings and synthetic pen-stroke thumbnails rather than boxes containing prose. This is a conceptual academic illustration, not an actual tested system or an image-editing service.

assets.purpose: Illustrative shared comparison setup, CNN and hybrid extractor alternatives, and regional score fusion.
assets.final_prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create an ORIGINAL publication-quality architecture illustration for a research proposal. The attached journal figure is a STYLE REFERENCE only: delicate technical outlines, perspective translucent salmon convolution feature maps, light green pooling planes, tall pale-gold feature vectors, muted lavender comparisons, white background. Do not copy its layer counts, tensor dimensions, topology or publication header.
Use the visual language of a real neural-network architecture plate, not a flowchart of rounded text boxes. Draw actual synthetic pen-stroke crops, dimensional feature tensors, token grids and embeddings. This is a conceptual candidate design, so do NOT invent numerical channel counts, vector dimensions, layer depths or performance results.
Compose three broad horizontal bands in a landscape 4:3 figure, with plenty of whitespace and large crisp labels:
TOP BAND title "Shared comparison setup". Two naturally different abstract pen-stroke inputs representing separate reference and query instances feed TWO identical-looking feature-extractor sequences (same weights, different inputs). Each produces its own gold feature vector. The vectors converge into one small comparison operation and one lavender pair score. Use small labels "Reference", "Query", "Shared weights", "Pair score". Neither input should be a person's readable name.
MIDDLE BAND contains TWO alternative extractors side by side, separated by whitespace, NOT connected in series.
Left title "A  CNN". One synthetic input goes through several salmon convolution slabs interleaved with small green pooling planes, then a pooling/projection symbol and a gold vector. Small labels "Convolutions", "Pooling", "Feature vector".
Right title "B  CNN–transformer hybrid". One input splits into an upper local CNN feature-map branch and a lower patch-grid plus self-attention token branch. Label them "Local CNN" and "Global attention". Their vectors converge into a concatenate/project operation labelled "Combine", producing ONE gold feature vector. Both branches start from the SAME full input; the global branch does not see only one local crop.
BOTTOM BAND title "Regional scoring". Exactly three corresponding reference–query region pairs, drawn as paired crop thumbnails with natural handwriting variation, produce exactly THREE lavender regional similarity bars. These bars feed a gold fusion column labelled "Equal or visibility weighting". A small burgundy reliability-map input feeds that fusion column, labelled "Visibility". The fused score is a neutral lavender output labelled "Combined score".
Do not show weights, scores or dimensions as numbers. No approval ticks or authenticity verdict. No output feeding backward into the model. All three bands communicate a proposed modular design: shared comparison, alternative extractor, optional regional fusion. Keep the figure beautifully legible and scientifically coherent at 16 cm print width, with perspective feature-map planes like the supplied example.
